findings.issue: getProfiles() returns email column for all requested users - any authenticated user can batch-request any user IDs and receive email addresses
findings.impact: Email addresses (direct PII identifiers) are exposed to all authenticated users via the profiles endpoint. No access scoping beyond authentication.
findings.fix: Remove email from the SELECT in getProfiles(). Only return display_name and avatar_url for non-owner requests.

findings.issue: GDPR account deletion does not clean up: audit_logs, consent_logs, webhook_endpoints, thread_metadata, thread_participants, channel_role_overrides, notification_preferences, webhook_deliveries
findings.impact: After 'deletion', user data persists in 8+ tables. Violates GDPR right to erasure (Article 17). Audit trail of the deletion itself is missing, making compliance non-demonstrable.
findings.fix: Add deletion queries for all missing tables. Create audit log entry recording the deletion. Wrap in transaction.

findings.issue: GDPR data export does not include: audit_logs, consent_logs, reactions, channel_members, webhook_endpoints, webhook_deliveries
findings.impact: Incomplete data portability. User receives partial data request and cannot verify what data is held about them.
findings.fix: Add queries for all missing data categories to the export endpoint

findings.issue: GDPR account deletion creates no audit log entry - deletion itself is invisible
findings.impact: Cannot demonstrate compliance with GDPR deletion requests. No record of when or by whom an account was deleted.
findings.fix: Call logAuditEvent before or after the deletion sequence, recording the deletion request

findings.issue: Rate limiter logs raw IP addresses via logger.warn on rate limit hits
findings.impact: IP addresses logged in plaintext. In EU jurisdictions, IP is considered PII. Accumulated rate-limit logs become a PII dataset without clear retention policy.
findings.fix: Hash or mask IP addresses before logging, or log only the subnet prefix (/24 for IPv4)

findings.issue: No data retention is actually running - all 6 pg_cron.schedule calls are commented out. Old PII (audit_logs with IP addresses, consent_logs) accumulates indefinitely.
findings.impact: Old audit_logs containing user IDs and IP addresses, and consent_logs with IP addresses and user agents, are never purged. Non-compliant with data minimization principle.
findings.fix: Enable pg_cron extension and activate data retention scheduling for audit_logs (90 days) and consent_logs (1 year)
